newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian job growth decelerating - trend.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian job growth decelerating - trend.

text.p: Australia's rate of job creation is decelerating, the Australian Bureau of Statistics' trend data shows.
Trend job growth rose from negative figures early in the year to a peak of 13,000 or 14,000 a month in the middle of the year to about 10,000 in September and 6,000 in October.
However, the latest seven trend figures, especially the latest one, are subject to revision.

The trend data shows part-time employment growth, around 4,000 jobs a month, is holding up more consistently than full-time, which has dipped from a mid-year rate of job creation of about 8,000 a month to 2,000 in October.
The trend unemployment rate is still rising, although the figure has been rounded to 8.7 percent in both of the latest two months.
